transcription_check.checked_by: Codex translation worker; same-agent review, no independent specialist review
transcription_check.evidence: Individually inspected all 20 Poppler page images /tmp/semetey1-volta-0695-0714/page-0695.png through page-0714.png, scale1600. Read left column then right column. All running titles, folios and printer signatures classified; all indented continuations grouped, preserving exact raw glyphs, IDs and bboxes. No fixed row assumption. Primary Kyrgyz/Russian Yudakhin dictionary and Kyrgyz editorial glossaries used only as lexical aids. No previous English poem translation used.
transcription_check.pair_review: All 1532 reconstructed Kyrgyz-English pairs read in source order: seven blocks of200 and final132. Initial lexical revisions were included in that full review; all twenty-two subsequent revised/held pairs separately reread against exact Kyrgyz. 18 whole unresolved verses excluded from English with complete source fragments and precise reasons. Every repetition retained. Narrative covers Burulcha’s Almambet recollection, Kulchoro’s abuse and reunion with Semetey, Kanykei’s gifts, Semetey’s proposed reconciliation and campaign, Bakai’s warning, the unrecognized Kardygach defeating Semetey, and her battle history. Miraculous claims, violent acts, hostile epithets, numbers and source inconsistencies preserved as narration; no expert certification.

alignment_check.scope: All source-English pairs and all revised pairs individually read. Final 1514 English verses have unique canonical first-source IDs; grouped fragments and explicit nonverse/unresolved exclusions account for every extraction record on PDF695–714 except20 watermarks.
